También enfatizó que se comunicará activamente con todas las partes, con la esperanza de promover la formación de reglas más claras y predecibles, evitando negar el derecho de los usuarios a utilizar razonablemente la IA de manera uniforme. excerpt_i18n.en: As generative AI fully enters the three-dimensional space, enabling machines not only to "see" objects but also to understand their structures, joints, and motion patterns has become a key focus for global research institutions and industries. From virtual content creation to robotic manipulation, and from digital twins to industrial simulation, the automated generation of movable 3D objects is regarded as a crucial foundational capability for future interactive digital worlds. However, existing methods are still largely constrained by reliance on complete 3D scans, inconsistencies arising from separate modeling of structure and texture, and difficulties in handling visibility changes caused by motion. In this context, a recent study by the S-Lab team at Nanyang Technological University offers a new solution. Their proposed unified modeling framework can generate movable 3D objects with realistic geometric structures, accurate joint parameters, and natural appearance textures from a single image, achieving significant improvements in geometric accuracy, appearance consistency, and motion plausibility. This work not only demonstrates the synergistic potential of structured latent spaces, diffusion-based 3D generation, and joint-aware texture modeling but also lays the groundwork for enhancing AI's understanding of object functionality and interactive attributes. Notably, one of the paper's authors, Pan Xingang, was an invited guest at the 2023 GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Conference, where he discussed cutting-edge directions in 3D vision, robotic manipulation, and generative models alongside researchers from top international institutions and companies.
